optionCases.a: The contract will only be awarded in mid-January; nothing has been awarded yet.
optionCases.b: Correct: the email opens by transmitting the tender calendar and walks through its stages and dates.
optionCases.c: The 10 November session is one detail in the calendar, and the email is addressed to her team, not to suppliers.
optionCases.d: The scoring is mentioned in one sentence (100 points, 70-point threshold) and is not explained in detail.

optionCases.a: The email requires all exchanges to go through the contracting authority, not direct email.
optionCases.b: The information session is an event for suppliers, not the required channel for all team exchanges.
optionCases.c: The 20 November deadline applies to suppliers' written questions, not to how the team communicates.
optionCases.d: Correct: 'tout échange avec les fournisseurs doit passer par l'autorité contractante'.

optionCases.a: Correct: 'attribuer le contrat' means awarding the contract to the selected supplier.
optionCases.b: Drafting the clauses is not what 'attribuer' means.
optionCases.c: It is the request for proposals that is published, not the contract.
optionCases.d: The estimated value is mentioned in the same sentence but is not what 'attribuer' means.

optionCases.a: Three weeks is how long the technical evaluation lasts.
optionCases.b: 20 November is the deadline for written questions.
optionCases.c: Correct: suppliers have 30 calendar days to submit their bids.
optionCases.d: Mid-January is the planned date for awarding the contract.

optionCases.a: Correct: 'celles' picks up 'Chaque soumission', the bids that are scored out of 100.
optionCases.b: Written questions are not scored and do not move on to the financial evaluation.
optionCases.c: The three weeks are how long the evaluation lasts; they are not scored and cannot reach a financial evaluation.
optionCases.d: Committee members' availability is mentioned later and has nothing to do with scoring.

optionCases.a: Termination is not announced; legal remedies are only to be examined if things do not improve.
optionCases.b: The installation of workstations is mentioned as a consequence of the delays, not explained.
optionCases.c: Correct: the note reports the supplier's delays and tells staff what to do in the meantime.
optionCases.d: The note asks staff to order earlier as a stopgap but does not blame them for the delays.

optionCases.a: 'La fin du mois' is when the supplier expects things to return to normal, not when the contract ends.
optionCases.b: Correct: 'les recours prévus au contrat' implies the contract has clauses the organisation could invoke if the supplier defaults.
optionCases.c: This contradicts the sentence, which refers to remedies provided for in the contract.
optionCases.d: The manufacturer is not a party to the contract and the note says nothing about holding it responsible.

optionCases.a: The note reports the supplier's explanation (a parts shortage) without calling it negligence.
optionCases.b: The note proposes concrete measures: ordering three weeks ahead and reporting delays.
optionCases.c: The note does not praise the supplier.
optionCases.d: Correct: it states the facts, relays the supplier's explanation and mentions possible remedies, a measured tone.

optionCases.a: The order is problem first and instructions later, not solution first.
optionCases.b: No other suppliers are compared.
optionCases.c: The note deals with a specific concrete case, not general rules.
optionCases.d: Correct: problem and its effects, the steps taken, the supplier's reply, instructions to staff, then a possible next step.

optionCases.a: Correct: 'puis nous lui avons envoyé un avis écrit lui demandant un plan de redressement'.
optionCases.b: No new call for tenders is mentioned.
optionCases.c: The manufacturer is only mentioned in the supplier's explanation; the team did not contact it.
optionCases.d: No financial penalty has been imposed; remedies are only to be examined later.

optionCases.a: 'Il demeure interdit' says splitting was already prohibited, not permitted.
optionCases.b: Correct: issuing a warning against splitting to stay under a threshold implies management sees the risk that some might do so.
optionCases.c: Nothing in the passage requires routine purchases to be grouped into one annual contract.
optionCases.d: The review is only hypothetical ('si elle était constatée, donnerait lieu'); no past cases are reported.

optionCases.a: No managers are replaced; 'relèvement' is not a 'relève' of staff.
optionCases.b: Tighter control is the opposite of what 'relèvement' refers to here; the passage stresses accountability separately.
optionCases.c: Correct: 'relèvement' is the raising of the threshold that managers can approve, from $25,000 to $40,000.
optionCases.d: No error in the earlier thresholds is mentioned.

optionCases.a: Correct: 'lesquels' (masculine plural) refers to 'achats courants', which made up nearly 60% of files.
optionCases.b: The thresholds are not in that clause, and thresholds are not files processed.
optionCases.c: Managers do not 'represent 60% of files processed'.
optionCases.d: Contracts over $100,000 are covered in the previous sentence and make no sense as 60% of routine files.

optionCases.a: The financial system records approvals; it does not grant them.
optionCases.b: The review committee is for contracts over $100,000.
optionCases.c: Cost centre managers can approve up to $40,000 only.
optionCases.d: Correct: between $40,000 and $100,000 the director general's approval remains required.

optionCases.a: The sentence says the opposite: the change is not a relaxation of controls.
optionCases.b: Correct: it warns managers that their wider authority does not exempt them from accountability.
optionCases.c: No apology is expressed.
optionCases.d: The writer expresses no doubt about the review.

optionCases.a: The team explicitly found no indication of fraud.
optionCases.b: The passage is about amendments after award, not contracts awarded without tendering.
optionCases.c: The passage accepts most amendments as justified and only recommends prior written justification above 50%.
optionCases.d: Correct: some post-award amendments lacked justification or approval in time, exposing the department to risk of challenge.

optionCases.a: Correct: numerical findings, then likely causes and risk, then a recommendation at the end.
optionCases.b: The recommendation comes last, not first.
optionCases.c: The two fiscal years are sampled together, not compared to show improvement.
optionCases.d: No complaints from suppliers are summarised; only the risk of a challenge is mentioned.

optionCases.a: The auditors found no sign of fraud, which rules out deliberate circumvention.
optionCases.b: Supplier pressure is not mentioned.
optionCases.c: Correct: the passage says the shortcomings 'semblent plutôt tenir à une méconnaissance des règles et à l'absence d'une liste de contrôle commune'.
optionCases.d: Staff shortages are not mentioned.

optionCases.a: No reimbursement by suppliers is mentioned or implied.
optionCases.b: Correct: signing after the work was done breaches the rule that no commitment may precede approval, so the department committed before approval.
optionCases.c: The passage does not say whether the four cases overlap with the seven.
optionCases.d: Nothing suggests the work was unnecessary; the problem is the timing of approval.

optionCases.a: The criterion is an increase of more than 50%, not a contract value over $50,000.
optionCases.b: $100,000 to $140,000 is a 40% increase, below the 50% threshold.
optionCases.c: Correct: $100,000 to $160,000 is a 60% increase, above 50%.
optionCases.d: Wrong because 'seulement' ignores increases between 50% and 100%, which the recommendation also covers.

optionCases.a: Correct: the letter confirms an intention to extend for six months under conditions and asks for a reply by 15 October.
optionCases.b: No termination is announced; the delays are a condition to correct.
optionCases.c: The new tender is mentioned only as the reason for the extension; there is no invitation.
optionCases.d: Rates are to stay unchanged unless the supplier documents higher costs; no increase is accepted.

optionCases.a: 'Savoir gré' expresses gratitude, not permission.
optionCases.b: It is a courteous request, not advice against something.
optionCases.c: A formal notice ('mise en demeure') is far stronger and legally loaded; 'savoir gré' is a polite formula.
optionCases.d: Correct: 'Nous vous saurions gré de' means 'we would be grateful if you would'.

optionCases.a: The meeting is in the first sentence and is not what is subject to conditions.
optionCases.b: Correct: 'Elle' takes up 'Cette prolongation', the subject of the previous sentence, and the conditions that follow concern the extension.
optionCases.c: 'La continuité du service' is feminine but sits inside a subordinate phrase; it is the purpose, not what is conditional.
optionCases.d: The supplier's team is mentioned later and is not subject to conditions.

optionCases.a: No immediate termination is threatened; 'd'autres options' is only a measured warning.
optionCases.b: The letter is formal throughout ('Madame', 'Veuillez agréer...').
optionCases.c: Correct: it praises the collaboration while setting firm conditions and a deadline.
optionCases.d: The intention to extend is confirmed; the conditions are not hesitation.

optionCases.a: Correct: 'certaines conditions' is announced, then set out under 'D'une part' and 'D'autre part'.
optionCases.b: The conditions are not ordered chronologically.
optionCases.c: Both conditions concern the supplier (documenting costs, correcting delays); there is no split with the department's obligations.
optionCases.d: The closing salutation contains no conditions.

optionCases.a: The passé composé presents a completed action and cannot express an ongoing action interrupted by the call.
optionCases.b: The present clashes with 'Hier' and the past-tense frame.
optionCases.c: Correct: the imparfait expresses the action in progress when the call ('m'a téléphoné') came.
optionCases.d: The future is impossible in a past narrative introduced by 'Hier'.

optionCases.a: Correct: 'bien que' takes the subjunctive, here 'ne soit pas encore terminé'.
optionCases.b: 'Bien que' with the indicative 'n'est' is a grammatical error.
optionCases.c: 'Malgré que' is criticised in formal writing and would in any case require the subjunctive, not 'n'est'.
optionCases.d: 'Même si' takes the indicative; 'même si ... soit' is a grammatical error.

optionCases.a: The plus-que-parfait with 'depuis' needs a past reference point, but the sentence is in the present ('connaît').
optionCases.b: 'Connaît' is correct; changing it leaves the 'a travaillé ... depuis' error in place.
optionCases.c: 'A connu' would be wrong and leaves the real error in place.
optionCases.d: Correct: an action still going on with 'depuis cinq ans' takes the present, 'travaille'.

optionCases.a: Nothing in the clause triggers the subjunctive; 'ait entraîné' is ungrammatical here.
optionCases.b: Correct: the past conditional reports an unverified fact, which fits 'Selon des renseignements encore non vérifiés'.
optionCases.c: The plus-que-parfait asserts the fact as certain and needs an earlier past reference point, which the sentence lacks.
optionCases.d: The error already happened during the last pay cycle, so the future does not fit.

optionCases.a: Si + present cannot be followed by the present conditional in the main clause.
optionCases.b: Correct: si + present indicative takes the simple future in the main clause.
optionCases.c: The past conditional belongs with si + plus-que-parfait and clashes with 'mois prochain'.
optionCases.d: The imparfait cannot express a future consequence of a si + present condition.

optionCases.a: 'Eût approuvé' is still a subjunctive (pluperfect), so the après que + subjunctive fault remains and the tense is literary.
optionCases.b: 'Pourra' is correct for a future main clause; changing it leaves the real error untouched.
optionCases.c: 'Puisse' would make the main clause ungrammatical and leaves the subjunctive after après que.
optionCases.d: Correct: après que takes the indicative, and the futur antérieur expresses anteriority to the future 'pourra'.

optionCases.a: Correct: the near future passive 'va être redémarré' fits 'dans dix minutes' and the urgent instruction.
optionCases.b: The passé composé contradicts 'dans dix minutes', a future time marker.
optionCases.c: The imparfait cannot refer to an event ten minutes in the future.
optionCases.d: The conditional presents the restart as hypothetical or hearsay, which contradicts the firm notice asking staff to save now.

optionCases.a: 'Fait' is indicative; 'il est essentiel que' requires the subjunctive.
optionCases.b: The future indicative is not allowed after an expression of necessity.
optionCases.c: Correct: 'il est essentiel que' takes the subjunctive 'fasse ... désigne'.
optionCases.d: The conditional is not allowed after 'il est essentiel que'.

optionCases.a: Correct: the literary passé simple is out of place in an email and clashes with the coordinated 'a confiné'; the passé composé aligns both verbs.
optionCases.b: The imparfait 'confinait' turns a completed action into a background state and leaves the passé simple.
optionCases.c: The plus-que-parfait would place the confinement before the discovery, which is illogical, and leaves 'constata'.
optionCases.d: The imparfait suits neither a punctual discovery nor the coordination with the passé composé.

optionCases.a: 'A été ouvert' calques the English 'has been open'; depuis + an ongoing state takes the present.
optionCases.b: Correct: depuis + a situation that is still going on takes the present indicative, consistent with 'réduit'.
optionCases.c: The imparfait would mean the situation is over, which contradicts 'ce qui réduit'.
optionCases.d: The future contradicts 'depuis le début du mois', which points to a state already under way.

optionCases.a: 'Pour que' requires the subjunctive, not the present indicative.
optionCases.b: The future indicative is ungrammatical after 'pour que'.
optionCases.c: The conditional is ungrammatical after 'pour que'.
optionCases.d: Correct: 'pour que' expresses purpose and takes the subjunctive 'puissent'.

optionCases.a: Changing the main clause leaves the forbidden si + conditional in place.
optionCases.b: 'Pouvions' breaks the main clause and leaves 'si ... recevrions'.
optionCases.c: Correct: si + imparfait ('recevions') pairs with the present conditional 'pourrions'.
optionCases.d: The future is also forbidden after hypothetical si and would not match 'pourrions'.

optionCases.a: The simple future breaks the sequence of tenses: June is now past and the plan was postponed, so the future in the past is required.
optionCases.b: The present does not express a future seen from a past announcement.
optionCases.c: Correct: the present conditional expresses the future in the past after 'avait annoncé que'.
optionCases.d: 'Annoncer que' takes the indicative, and the past subjunctive makes no sense here.

optionCases.a: 'À moins que' requires the subjunctive, not the present indicative.
optionCases.b: Correct: 'à moins que' takes the subjunctive, here with the optional ne explétif.
optionCases.c: The future indicative is ungrammatical after 'à moins que'.
optionCases.d: The conditional is ungrammatical after 'à moins que'.

optionCases.a: Correct: affirmative 'croire que' takes the indicative, so 'soit' becomes 'est'.
optionCases.b: 'Croie' would put a subjunctive in an independent main clause, which is ungrammatical, and leaves 'soit'.
optionCases.c: Changing the tense of 'croit' does not remove the wrong subjunctive in the subordinate clause.
optionCases.d: 'Fût' is still a subjunctive, and a literary imperfect one that breaks the sequence of tenses.

optionCases.a: 'Il faut que' requires the subjunctive, not the passé composé.
optionCases.b: The futur antérieur is indicative and ungrammatical after 'il faut que'.
optionCases.c: The conditional is ungrammatical after 'il faut que'.
optionCases.d: Correct: the past subjunctive 'ait coupé' follows 'il faut que', and its auxiliary also carries the participle 'apposé'.

optionCases.a: Correct: the imparfait describes the state at the time of the incident, and the plus-que-parfait marks the earlier non-installation.
optionCases.b: The passé composé presents the wet floor as an event rather than the background state that 'au moment de' calls for.
optionCases.c: The passé simple is literary, out of place in an investigation report, and also treats the state as an event.
optionCases.d: The future contradicts a past incident.

optionCases.a: The indicative after 'de sorte que' marks an achieved result, but this is the intended goal of a recommended change, which takes the subjunctive.
optionCases.b: Correct: 'de sorte que' expressing purpose takes the present subjunctive, matching the present 'recommande'.
optionCases.c: The imparfait indicative states neither a purpose nor a present result.
optionCases.d: 'Pussent' is a literary imperfect subjunctive that breaks the sequence of tenses after a present main verb.

optionCases.a: The plus-que-parfait cannot serve as the main clause of a si + plus-que-parfait conditional.
optionCases.b: The futur antérieur does not express an unreal past consequence.
optionCases.c: The subjunctive has no place in the main clause of a conditional sentence.
optionCases.d: Correct: si + plus-que-parfait takes the past conditional, 'aurait été rejetée'.

optionCases.a: The imparfait contradicts 'dans dix jours ouvrables', a future time marker.
optionCases.b: The past conditional implies an unreal past, which contradicts the future time frame.
optionCases.c: Correct: 'dans dix jours' calls for the simple future, 'prendra fin ... ne sera acceptée'.
optionCases.d: The passé composé contradicts the future time frame.

optionCases.a: 'Il manquait' correctly describes a background state, so the passé composé would be wrong.
optionCases.b: Correct: the noticing is a punctual completed action ('immédiatement'), so it takes the passé composé, like 'avons reçu'.
optionCases.c: The futur antérieur contradicts the past narration and leaves 'remarquions'.
optionCases.d: The present breaks the past sequence of tenses.

optionCases.a: Correct: the near future 'va le soumettre' matches 'demain matin' and 'pas encore diffusé'.
optionCases.b: 'Vient de' is the recent past and contradicts 'demain matin'.
optionCases.c: The passé composé of 'aller' places the action in the past and contradicts 'demain matin'.
optionCases.d: The recent past in the imparfait contradicts both the present frame and 'demain matin'.

optionCases.a: The plus-que-parfait states a fact, but 'Sans l'intervention...' introduces an unreal past.
optionCases.b: The futur antérieur of conjecture does not express an unreal consequence.
optionCases.c: Correct: an implicit past counterfactual ('Sans X') takes the past conditional 'aurait circulé'.
optionCases.d: The present conditional does not fit a completed past period ('fin de semaine dernière').

optionCases.a: The present 'affirme' clashes with 'du mois dernier' and the past 'a fait', and leaves the concordance problem.
optionCases.b: The present does not express a future seen from a past statement.
optionCases.c: 'Affirmer que' takes the indicative, and the past subjunctive makes no sense here.
optionCases.d: Correct: after a past main verb, a future that has since come to pass ('ce qu'il a fait') takes the conditional 'publierait'.

optionCases.a: 'Dès que' takes the indicative, not the subjunctive.
optionCases.b: The conditional does not express a future completed before another future action.
optionCases.c: The plus-que-parfait is a past tense and contradicts the future 'présentera'.
optionCases.d: Correct: the futur antérieur marks an action completed before the future main action 'présentera'.

optionCases.a: Correct: 'dès que' with a future main clause takes the future indicative.
optionCases.b: The conditional does not match the future main verb 'pourrons'.
optionCases.c: The imparfait contradicts the future time frame.
optionCases.d: 'Dès que' takes the indicative; the subjunctive is a common error.

optionCases.a: This would make both verbs past, which contradicts 'La semaine prochaine'.
optionCases.b: The plus-que-parfait contradicts the future time marker.
optionCases.c: Correct: 'La semaine prochaine' calls for the near future, matching 'va répondre'.
optionCases.d: The imparfait contradicts the future time marker.

optionCases.a: The imparfait would suggest a habitual or ongoing action, whereas joining the public service is a single completed event.
optionCases.b: Correct: the passé composé marks the punctual event against which the imparfait 'étaient' sets the background.
optionCases.c: The plus-que-parfait implies anteriority to another past reference point that the sentence does not supply.
optionCases.d: The future contradicts 'il y a une dizaine d'années'.

optionCases.a: Correct: affirmative 'espérer que' takes the indicative, here the future for sessions starting in January.
optionCases.b: The subjunctive after affirmative 'espérer' is non-standard.
optionCases.c: The past subjunctive is both the wrong mood and the wrong time for sessions that have not yet started.
optionCases.d: The imparfait contradicts the future time frame ('commenceront en janvier').

optionCases.a: 'A été' is still indicative, and the concessive 'quoique' requires the subjunctive.
optionCases.b: 'Connaissent' is correct; changing it breaks the present frame and leaves the real error.
optionCases.c: 'Quoi que' means 'whatever' and would make the sentence ungrammatical.
optionCases.d: Correct: 'quoique' takes the subjunctive, so 'est' becomes 'soit'.

optionCases.a: 'Avant que' requires the subjunctive, not the indicative.
optionCases.b: The future indicative is ungrammatical after 'avant que'.
optionCases.c: Correct: 'avant que' takes the subjunctive 'soit mis' (the ne explétif is optional).
optionCases.d: The conditional is ungrammatical after 'avant que'.

optionCases.a: The future follows si + present, not si + imparfait.
optionCases.b: Correct: si + imparfait takes the present conditional in the main clause.
optionCases.c: The present indicative does not express the hypothetical consequence of si + imparfait.
optionCases.d: The subjunctive is ungrammatical in this main clause.

optionCases.a: Correct: 'à condition que' (repeated as 'que') takes the subjunctive, here the past subjunctive for a prior action.
optionCases.b: 'Approuve' is already a correct subjunctive; the future indicative would introduce an error.
optionCases.c: 'Pourront' is correct for a firm future entitlement; the error is in the subordinate clause.
optionCases.d: The future indicative is still the wrong mood after 'à condition que'.
